record.original_question: Is there a constant k such that every 2-connected cubic graph embedded in a surface with face-width at least k is 3-edge-colourable?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 Is there a number k such that any 2-connected cubic graph embedded on a surface with face-width at least k is 3-edge-colourable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected cubic (3-regular) graph. Suppose $G$ is 2-cell embedded in a closed surface $\Sigma$ (orientable or non-orientable). The face-width (or representativity) of such an embedding is defined as the minimum number of intersection points of $G$ with a non-contractible simple closed curve on $\Sigma$, where the minimum is taken over all such curves.

A 3-edge-colouring of $G$ is an assignment of three colours to the edges of $G$ such that any two edges sharing a vertex receive distinct colours.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $k$ (independent of the surface and the graph) such that every 2-connected cubic graph admitting an embedding in some surface with face-width at least $k$ admits a 3-edge-colouring?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a conjecture attributed to Mohar and Robertson (1988), listed on Mohar's open problems page as still conjectural. While there has been recent progress on related conjectures (Grünbaum's conjecture for the torus and the projective plane has been settled by Robertson-Seymour-Thomas style work and recent preprints), the question of whether a universal face-width constant k suffices across all surfaces does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Grünbaum's Edge-Coloring Conjecture (Mohar)
status_evidence.snippet: There is a fixed constant k such that every 2-connected cubic graph with an (orientable) embedding of face-width at least k has a 3-edge-coloring.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open conjecture on Mohar's problem page.

status_evidence.title: Three-edge-coloring (Tait coloring) cubic graphs on the torus
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of Grünbaum's conjecture for the torus.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on a related but distinct (polyhedral embedding) version of the problem.
